newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr edges lower by late Tokyo as market rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Dlr edges lower by late Tokyo as market rates rise.

text.p: The dollar gave up its earlier gains against the yen by late Tokyo on Wednesday, prompted by rises in Japan's market interest rates, dealers said.

The dollar's inability to rise above 117 yen also encouraged sales, in line with mark sales against yen. But dealers said a sharp dollar fall is unlikely due to little fear of a rise in Japan's official interest rates any time soon.
The yield of the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond rose as high as 2.7 percent, up from 2.645 percent on Tuesday.

The rise was in part due to Standard & Poor's assignment of poor ratings to some medium-sized Japanese life insurers, which led to speculation of possible selling of yen bonds by the life insurers, dealers said.
"The dollar was depressed by rises in yen interest rates, but it is unlikely to lose ground due to the slim prospect that Japan's official rates will be raised soon," said a bank dealer.
Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said that the bank wants to make sure that the recovery will be sustainable.
Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday that the economic recovery is getting firmer despite effects from a rise in the sales tax, and the recovery is likely to continue.
But he added: "For the time being we will continue to carry out monetary policy putting emphasis on strengthening the basis of the economic recovery."

The greenback rose as high as 117.00 yen in morning trade, on the back of mark buying against the yen. The mark had fallen sharply overseas due to renewed concern about a single European currency. But the German currency fell back against the yen in afternoon trade, which pushed the dollar/yen down in tandem.
"The mark is not a good currency to buy because of worries about a weak euro," said a Tokyo dealer. The mark was standing at around 68.20 yen at 0716 GMT, down from 68.48 yen at midday.

French National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin said on Tuesday that he favoured looser criteria and a larger number of entrants in the first round of European monetary union. Seguin is seen as a potential successor to Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who on Monday announced his decision to resign.
Concern about a weak single European currency and expectations of higher U.S. interest rates have helped to support dollar sentiment.

"At the moment, the dollar/yen is not the centre of market players' interest. People are more interested in what indirect impact European currencies might have on the yen ahead of the second round of French elections," said a trust bank trader.
The dollar steadied on the mark in late trade, with trading confined to a narrow band throughout the day in Tokyo.

"The dollar/mark is pretty range-bound at the moment. It's a matter of mark/yen and sterling/mark play," said a dealer in Singapore, adding that the dollar/mark was confined in a 1.7030 to 1.7080 range. ---Singapore newsroom (65-8703080) ---Tatsuo Ito in Tokyo 81-3-3432-1396
